method: Rigid-tree geometry with whole-body center of mass and exact box/capsule support extents; vertically translate the fixed pose until its lowest geometry touches the floor. Compare the same pose at adjacent orientations and retain the entire sampled height population.
selection_provenance: All sixteen bodies are inherited from the feedback cohort. A posthoc exploratory screen of 6,561 factored poses on S169 motivated this larger diagnostic; neither the pose bank nor these bodies are held out.
qualification_economy: New observable: whole-body floor-supported center-of-mass height across joint poses and orientations. The existing fixed-base distal-reach screen cannot express this. One shared unversioned module consumes declarations and reuses RigidTree plus contained_stage_owner_v2; no native campaign gate or historical audit is duplicated.
limits: Finite sampled geometry only; no continuous pose, orientation or morphology coverage.
Each five-degree comparison holds its joint pose fixed. Transitions between selected witness poses, their joint work and contact-force feasibility are not modeled.
The lowest collision point is placed at the floor by free vertical translation. This is a geometric support convention, not a dynamic contact solution, energy barrier bound or executable trajectory.
Momentum, collision losses, joint-speed limits, force caps and self-intersection during motion are not evaluated by this screen. Native models and physical limits remain unchanged.
Observed native angles summarize original controller boundaries, not every internal solver step; they are posthoc and do not relabel any original eligibility outcome.
Ascending intervals for every sampled pose do not prove righting impossibility. A descending sample does not establish feasible motion or recovery.
No new physics world, learning update, acceptance, Tier 2, Tier 3 or release authority.
